22 What is the relationship between the amplitude of a wave and its intensity?
A
amplitude ∝ intensity
B
amplitude ∝ (intensity)2
C
amplitude ∝ intensity
D
(amplitude)2 ∝
intensity

hints: Notice the question asks how amplitude depends on intensity, and all options use $\propto$ with intensity or $\sqrt{\text{intensity}}$.
Recall the governing rule for waves that intensity is proportional to the square of the amplitude, $I \propto A^2$.
Rearrange $I \propto A^2$ to make amplitude the subject by taking the square root of both sides.
walkthrough: Identify the definitions: amplitude $A$ is the maximum displacement, intensity $I$ is power per unit area.
State the physical rule for a progressive wave: the energy carried is proportional to $A^2$, so $I \propto A^2$.
The options write amplitude as the subject, so rearrange by taking the square root: $A \propto \sqrt{I}$.
Check against the options: doubling amplitude makes intensity four times larger, which matches $A \propto \sqrt{I}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Intensity is not directly proportional to amplitude, it increases faster than amplitude because $I \propto A^2$.

B.explanation: This reverses the square relationship - intensity is proportional to $(\text{amplitude})^2$, not the other way round.

C.explanation: Since $I \propto A^2$, taking the square root gives $A \propto \sqrt{I}$.

D.explanation: Since $(\text{amplitude})^2 \propto \text{intensity}$, it cannot also be proportional to $\sqrt{\text{intensity}}$.
